description: Step-by-step diagnostic workflows for common Loxone Miniserver troubleshooting scenarios. Each scenario lists symptoms, the sequence of MCP resources and tools to use, and how to interpret results.

steps.description: Read aggregated health snapshot
steps.interpret: Check plc.healthy (should be true, state=5=running). cpuHealthy=false means >80% CPU load. heapHealthy=false means <10000 bytes free — instability risk. Review firmwareVersion against latest release. Any unhealthy flag warrants further investigation.

scenarios.title: PLC Stopped or in Error State

steps.description: Confirm PLC state via aggregated health snapshot
steps.interpret: Check plc.state and plc.healthy. 7 = error, 0 = not started. If plc.healthy is false, proceed.

steps.description: Check system log for the error
steps.interpret: Look for ERROR or WARN lines near the timestamp when problems started.

steps.description: If PLC is stopped, try resuming
steps.interpret: Resumes the PLC after a stop. Re-check loxone://system/status afterwards.

steps.description: If resume fails, restart the PLC
steps.interpret: Full PLC restart. Controls will be temporarily unavailable. Check state again after 10-15 seconds.

steps.description: If still failing, reboot the Miniserver
steps.caution: This disconnects all clients. Only do this if PLC restart did not help.

scenarios.title: Specific Control Not Responding
symptoms: One control does not react to commands
operate_control returns success but nothing happens

steps.description: Get current state of the control
steps.interpret: Check if statesAvailable is true. If false, state updates may not be streaming — enableStateUpdates may be needed.

steps.description: Cross-check state via MCP device state resource
steps.interpret: Verify statesAvailable and compare state values. If no states, state streaming may not be active.

steps.description: List PLC outputs to find the control's physical output
steps.interpret: Returns all output names and UUIDs. Find the control's outputs and verify they are listed.

steps.description: Check all physical hardware devices for offline status
steps.interpret: Look for devices where Online=0. An offline extension would explain why controls on it don't work.

steps.description: Review recent log entries for errors related to this control

scenarios.title: Finding Offline or Disconnected Hardware
symptoms: Some devices or extensions not responding
Controls in a specific room all stopped working

steps.description: List all physical devices including offline ones
steps.interpret: Devices with Online=0 are disconnected. Note the Serial number of offline devices.

steps.description: Get full hardware status XML for more detail
steps.interpret: Full XML with all extensions and their states. More detailed than the physical devices resource.

steps.description: List all PLC devices for extension inventory
steps.interpret: All devices registered in the PLC. Cross-reference with loxone://devices to find gaps.

steps.description: Try rebooting a specific offline extension (replace SERIAL with actual serial)
steps.interpret: Sends a reboot command to the extension. Wait 30 seconds and re-check loxone://devices.

steps.description: For Tree/Air devices, try rebooting the device
steps.interpret: Reboots a Tree bus or Air wireless device. Use the device serial from loxone://devices.

scenarios.title: Reviewing System Logs for Errors
symptoms: Need to find when an event occurred

steps.description: Get the last 200 lines of the system log
steps.interpret: Look for lines containing ERROR, WARN, or unusual messages. Timestamps help narrow down when issues started.

steps.description: Get more log history if needed
steps.interpret: Increase the line count for more history. The log rotates so very old entries may not be available.

steps.description: Check system statistics for historical load info
steps.interpret: System-level statistics. Complements the log with numeric performance data.

scenarios.title: Investigating Energy or Sensor Statistics
symptoms: Need to analyze historical sensor data

steps.description: Find all controls that have statistics configured
steps.interpret: Lists all controls with statistic or statisticV2 configured. Note the UUIDs of controls you want to analyze.

steps.description: Fetch statistics for a specific control
steps.interpret: Returns time-series data. unit can be HOUR, DAY, MONTH, or YEAR. Adjust date range as needed.

steps.description: Fetch statistics for multiple controls in one request
steps.interpret: Repeat uuid/from/to triples for each control. All must have matching counts.

steps.description: Read full network configuration from aggregated health snapshot
steps.interpret: Check network.ip, network.dns, and network.ntp. Also review system.systemTime to verify NTP is working correctly. Incorrect IP or DNS explains connectivity and cloud service failures.

steps.description: Force NTP resync if time is wrong
steps.interpret: Forces an immediate NTP synchronization. Re-read loxone://system/status afterwards to confirm system.systemTime updated.
